Title: High blood pressure raises the risk of stroke by 25%
NewsSummary: Effective control of blood pressure can reduce the risk of stroke by 25 per cent.
NewsContent:
Effective control of blood pressure can reduce the risk of stroke by 25 per cent. This was a major outcome of the public awareness programme held to mark the "World Stroke Day" jointly organised by Aga Khan University (AKU) and Pakistan Stroke Society at AKU on April 16.

Dr Nadir Ali Syed informed the audience that more than 350,000 people suffer from stroke every year in Pakistan. More than 70% of these stroke patients have high blood pressure. High blood pressure is a major risk factor which is present in more than 30% of the population above the age of 45.

Dr Shahid Mustafa, consultant Neurologist said that stroke is a preventable disease. Studies have shown that even reducing 3 mm diastolic blood pressure could reduce stroke risk by 25%." Blood pressure control and exercise is the key to stroke prevention, he said.

Dr Mughis Sheerani, Assistant Professor of Neurology informed the audience that death rate and disability due to stroke could be significantly reduced by post stroke care. If the patient is admitted in a stroke care unit, the outcome is better. The whole family has to be involved in post stroke care.

Dr Ayesha Kamal said that about a quarter of the patients could return to work if properly treated. Stroke services at AKU start in the emergency room and continue with rehabilitation after discharge.

Dr Nabila Soomro, Consultant Rehabilitation Specialist said that rehabilitation should start early and first 4-6 weeks are most important. Dr Naeem Siddiqui from Department of Psychiatry emphasised the importance of treating depression in stroke patients. In the end, a panel of experts responded to questions from the public.

As a part of its social responsibility and commitment to the advancement of health research and education, AKU regularly holds seminars, symposiums and events to raise awareness about health and education related issues which are of national importance and interest.
